literal: Even if one evil word's harmful consequence arises, goodness will end up becoming non-existent.
translation: If even a single evil word spoken causes harmful consequences, all the other good done by a person will become completely ruined.
modern: பேசும் சொற்களில் ஒன்றே ஒன்று தீய சொல்லாக இருந்து, அதனால் தீய விளைவு ஏற்பட்டால், ஒருவருடைய மற்ற நன்மைகள் அனைத்தும் பயனில்லாமல் போய்விடும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the extreme caution needed in speech as part of self-control. The author warns that even if a person has practiced great virtue and done much good, a single slip of the tongue that causes harm (தீச்சொல் பொருட்பயன்) can completely destroy the merit of all those good deeds. The phrase 'poruṭpayaṉ' refers to the actual harmful consequence or sting carried by the meaning of the word. Therefore, self-restraint must be absolute, as even a single lapse in speech can undo a lifetime of goodness.
